encoding_variations: 'Commitment' (East coast) vs 'Preliminary Report' (West coast) for the same document
Schedule numbering varies: A/B-I/B-II vs A/B/C; some use 'Requirements' and 'Exceptions' without letters
Vesting recitals are formulaic but wordy: 'John Smith and Mary Smith, husband and wife, as joint tenants with right of survivorship'
Legal descriptions: lot-and-block (short), metes-and-bounds (very long), condo (unit + building + declaration reference)

open_questions.q: Legal description length vs the token ceiling
open_questions.recommendation: verbatim — TI-2 compares text, and a truncation would produce false mismatches. But test against a metes-and-bounds commitment plus two nested lists

open_questions.q: Requirements and exceptions merged with a discriminator, or two lists?
open_questions.recommendation: one list — saves ~5 plumbing sites, and the discriminator preserves the distinction rules depend on

open_questions.q: A lien appearing in BOTH requirements and exceptions
open_questions.recommendation: capture both — TI-3 needs the requirement to see the payoff plan; TI-4 needs the exception to see the encumbrance

open_questions.q: APN vs address as the match key for TI-1/PR-7/RE-1
options: prefer the APN where both documents carry one
open_questions.recommendation: capture the APN regardless; preferring it is a RULE change, not a schema one

open_questions.q: Defer chain_of_title (~5 sites, serves only TI-6/FR-2)?
open_questions.recommendation: ship schedule_b_items first — it unblocks TI-3, TI-4 and CR-11; chain_of_title serves two AI-surface rules

notes: NO v2 catalog entry — the rule floor IS the entire schema. Every field is rule_floor: true.
Second-largest unlock after the credit report: 10 of its 14 rules are BLOCKED on this extractor.
Schedule B-I Requirements are conditions to satisfy before closing; B-II Exceptions are coverage carve-outs. Merging them would break TI-3, which reads requirements for the payoff plan.
